message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide you can follow (or hand off to your DBA) to bring a brand‑new Microsoft SQL Server into operation at `http://plgah.ca`. Feel free to adapt each section to match your environment’s naming conventions, compliance requirements, or automation tooling. --- ### 1️⃣ Verify Network & DNS | Item | What to check | |------|---------------| | **DNS resolution** | From a machine inside your corporate LAN run `nslookup plgah.ca` – it should return the public IP address of the host where the DB will live. If you’re using Azure/AWS/Google Cloud, make sure the hostname resolves correctly from all VMs that’ll connect. | | **Firewall / NSG** | Ensure inbound TCP port **1433** (default MSSQL) is open between client subnets/VPCs and the target VM/subnet. For Azure, this means creating an *Inbound Port Rule* allowing traffic on 1433. | | **Outbound** | Clients may also require outbound HTTPS/TCP ports for driver updates or monitoring agents. | > ⚠️ **Tip:** Use private endpoints or VPN gateways instead of exposing the server directly over the internet whenever possible. --- ### 2️⃣ Provision the Host Machine | Platform | Typical Steps | |----------|--------------| | **Windows Server** | • Install Windows Server 2019/2022.
• Apply latest cumulative updates.
• Create a dedicated “sql” service account (`DOMAIN\SqlSvc`).
• Disable unnecessary services (e.g., IIS unless required). | | **Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)** | • Update packages (`apt-get update && apt-get upgrade -y`).
• Add the Microsoft repository:
curl https://packages.microsoft.com/config/ubuntu/22.04/prod.list > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/mssql-server.list
wget -qO- https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc | sudo apt-key add -

• Install mssql‑server (`sudo apt-get install -y mssql-server`). | | **Azure Virtual Machines** | • Pick a size with enough vCPU/RAM for expected load.
• Enable Managed Identity if you plan to use Key Vault secrets later. | After provisioning: ```bash # On Linux: sudo /opt/mssql/bin/sqlservr --accept-eula ``` On Windows, launch the **SQL Server Installation Center**, choose *New installation or add features to an existing installation*, then select the appropriate edition (Developer/Test vs Standard/Evaluation). --- ### 3️⃣ Configure SQL Server Instance #### A. Basic Setup Wizard (GUI) 1. **Instance Configuration** - Choose *Named instance* (recommended) → e.g., `PLGAH`. - Set the service account to the one created earlier. 2. **Database Engine Configuration** - Mixed Mode Authentication + enable SQL login `sa` (set strong password). - Optionally disable `sa` after initial setup and rely solely on Windows Auth. 3. **Reporting Services** (optional) - Skip if you don’t need SSRS. 4. **Advanced Options** - Set collation to `Latin1_General_CI_AS` (unless you have special needs). 5. Finish wizard, let the engine start automatically. #### B. Command Line (PowerShell / Bash) ```powershell $instanceName = "PLGAH" $sqlSysAdminPassword = Read-Host -AsSecureString "Enter SA Password" Install-SqlSetup ` -Edition Developer ` -InstanceName $instanceName ` -SecurityMode Mixed ` -SaPassword $sqlSysAdminPassword ` -UpdateEnabled True ` -AcceptEULA ``` For Linux: ```bash sudo ACCEPT_EULA=Y MSSQL_PID=Developer \ ./install.sh ``` --- ### 4️⃣ Harden Security Settings | Setting | Why It Matters | How To Do It | |---------|-----------------|-------------| | **Enable Transparent Data Encryption (TDE)** | Protect data-at-rest against physical theft. | In SSMS ➜ right-click Database ➜ Properties ➜ TDE ➜ Enable. | | **Configure Auditing** | Log successful/failure logins, schema changes. | `CREATE SERVER AUDIT ...`; attach to event types. | | **Set Connection Timeout** | Prevent long‑running idle connections. | Edit `max_connections`, `remote_query_timeout`. | | **Use Always Encrypted** | Encrypt sensitive columns end‑to‑end. | Generate column master key, column encryption keys via SSMS. | | **Restrict Public Access** | Only allow known clients/IP ranges. | Firewall rule + IPSEC policy. | --- ### 5️⃣ Create Databases & Users ```sql -- Example: Create a production database USE [master]; GO CREATE DATABASE MyAppDB ON PRIMARY ( NAME='MyAppDB_data', FILENAME='C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL15.MSSQLSERVER\MSSQL\Data\MyAppDB.mdf' ), FILEGROUP MyDataFG ( NAME='MyAppDB_log', FILENAME='C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL15.MSSQLSERVER\MSSQL\Data\MyAppDB.ldf' ); GO -- Grant permissions to application pool identity GRANT CONNECT TO DOMAIN\AppPoolUser; ALTER ROLE db_owner ADD MEMBER DOMAIN\AppPoolUser; GO ``` If you prefer Windows auth only, skip enabling mixed mode and simply grant rights to domain accounts. --- ### 6️⃣ Test Connectivity From a client box: ```cmd sqlcmd -S plgah.ca\,1433 -U sa -P YourStrong!Passw0rd -Q "SELECT @@VERSION;" ``` Or using .NET Core: ```csharp var connStr = @"Server=tcp:plgah.ca,1433;Initial Catalog=MyAppDB;Persist Security Info=False;" + @"User ID=sa;Password=YourStrong!Passw0rd;MultipleActiveResultSets=True;"; using var cnx = new SqlConnection(connStr); cnx.Open(); Console.WriteLine("Connected!"); ``` Verify latency (<50 ms), error handling, and retry logic. --- ### 7️⃣ Backup Strategy | Frequency | Retention | Storage Location | |-----------|------------|-------------------| | Full | Daily | Local disk + Offsite (Blob storage, S3, or Azure Recovery Services vault) | | Differential | Weekly | Same as above | | Transaction Log | Hourly | Same as above | Automate backups with PowerShell scripts or native SQL Agent jobs: ```ps Invoke-SqlBackup @( @{Database="MyAppDB"; Type="Full"} ) ``` Schedule them during low‑traffic windows. --- ### 8️⃣ Monitoring & Alerting | Tool | Purpose | |------|--------| | **SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)** | Manual queries, performance tuning. | | **SQL Server Profiler / Extended Events** | Capture problematic queries. | | **Prometheus + Grafana** | Export metrics via `mssql_exporter`. | | **Azure Monitor / AWS RDS Performance Insights** | Native cloud dashboards. | | **Custom Alerts** | CPU >80%, Disk I/O >90% for X minutes, failed logins > Y per hour. | Example Prometheus exporter command line: ```bash ./mssql-exporter.exe -config.file=mssql.yml ``` Where `mssql.yml` contains credentials stored securely (KeyVault, Secrets Manager). --- ### 9️⃣ Documentation Checklist - **Hostname/IP** – `plgah.ca` - **Port** – `1433` - **Instance Name** – `PLGAH` - **Authentication Method** – Mixed Mode (SA disabled post‑setup) - **Service Account** – `DOMAIN\SqlSvc` - **Databases Created** – List names, owners, file paths - **Users & Roles** – Domain groups mapped to roles - **Backups** – Schedule, retention, location - **Monitoring** – Dashboards URLs, alert thresholds - **Disaster Recovery Plan** – Restore procedure tested Store this doc in Confluence/Jira/SharePoint so everyone knows who owns what. --- ### 🔧 Quick Reference Snippets #### Connection String (ADO.NET) ```text Server=tcp:plgah.ca,1433;Database=MyAppDB;Encrypt=true;TrustServerCertificate=false; User Id=myDomain\UserGroup;Password=SecretPwd123!; ApplicationIntent=ReadWrite;MultiSubnetFailover=yes; ``` #### PowerShell Script to Restart Service ```powershell Restart-Service -Name MssqlServer ``` #### Bash One‑liner to Check Health ```bash echo "select status_desc from sys.dm_server_services where servicename='MSSQLSERVER';" | sqlcmd -S tcp:plgah.ca,1433 -U sa -P YourStrong!Passw0rd ``` --- ### 📌 Final Thoughts - Keep the OS patched—apply critical updates weekly. - Rotate passwords regularly; consider integrating with AD/Kerberos. - Review logs monthly for suspicious activity. - Run periodic restore drills to validate recovery time objectives (RTO). Once everything passes the smoke tests, you’ve successfully added a new SQL Server at `http://plgah.ca`. Let me know if you’d like deeper dives into any particular area (performance tuning, high availability, containerization, etc.).
